phase_name: HATP Hardware-Credential Admin Recovery Authority Narrow Repair
phase_title: HATP Hardware-Credential Admin Recovery Authority Narrow Repair
recommended_next_phase: 149O.20L.7O.2L.4 -- independent verification of the recovery-authority repair. Must independently confirm no public recover/import route exists, fabricated credential evidence cannot be persisted through any CLI path, provider-derived enrollment remains intact, safe failure/retry semantics hold, and no authority regression elsewhere (principal/signer script, revoke). Do not proceed to HMIC v1.7 source-scope evolution until 2L.4 closes this Blocking finding.
summary: Phase 149O.20L.7O.2L.3 is a narrow repair phase (no real Trust-Enrollment effect performed; no HHCE-001/HPSE-001 contract change; no core writer change; no HMIC amendment). It repairs the sole Blocking finding independently verified by 149O.20L.7O.2L.2 (HARDWARE-ENROLLMENT RECOVERY AUTHORITY DEFECT): scripts/hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py exposed a public recover subcommand accepting fully human-typed credential identity with zero binding to any actual completed hardware ceremony, persisted as an authoritative HardwareCredentialRecord. Before editing, primary source was independently re-read: HHCE-001 v1.1 (confirming HHCE-REQ-015 names exactly register_credential/revoke_credential, no third operation, and HHCE-REQ-016's idempotency makes an identical-evidence retry always safe), the 149O.20L.7O.2L architecture-freeze document (confirming its own section 6 already specifies a sufficient in-process retry model requiring no new external-input surface -- 'no additional recovery state machine is required ... not by a new mechanism this phase needs to invent'), and the pre-repair script/core-writer source directly. Repair decision: remove recover entirely rather than amend HHCE-001/the architecture, because no primary evidence demonstrates an external human-entry recovery path is required -- 2L.2's own finding is precisely that 2L.1 built an unauthorized path instead of the already-specified retry, not that the retry was insufficient. Exact source change: scripts/hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py had the recover argparse subcommand, its five CLI arguments, the _cmd_recover dispatch function, the recover branch in main(), and _print_recovery_evidence (which printed full credential material for manual re-entry) all removed; a new _register_with_in_process_retry(*, repository_root, evidence) helper was added, called from _cmd_enroll in place of the single register_credential() call -- a bounded (3-attempt) retry loop reusing the identical CredentialEnrollmentEvidence object one ceremony call already produced, never re-touching hardware, never accepting caller-supplied identity, printing a diagnostic naming no credential material on exhaustion. No core writer module, contract file, or the principal/signer script was modified (git-diff-asserted byte-identical since phase entry). Public CLI is now exactly enroll/revoke; any recover invocation fails at argparse parsing (SystemExit 2) before any provider/writer call. 27 new independently-authored tests were written covering: recover-removed proof, no-caller-supplied-identity-import-surface proof (mechanical argparse search plus an explicit fabricated-evidence-cannot-be-submitted test), single-ceremony-call-count proof even under a flaky write, the full hardware-success/persistence-failure matrix (never-landed write lands on retry, already-landed write resolves idempotently, genuine conflict fails closed after exhausting retries, exhausted-retries diagnostic names no credential material), revoke regression, principal/signer-script-unchanged proof, no-core-writer/contract-change proof, thin-wrapper-invariant proof (AST-enumerated call allowlist on the new retry helper), fresh HMIC-REQ-052 analysis (both scripts still answer YES; frozen set unchanged at 36; future delta unchanged at 38), and confirmation zero-touch preservation. 27/27 pass. 2L/2L.1/2L.2's own recover-asserting tests were updated in place, not deleted, per the governing instruction to preserve historical exploit evidence: tests/test_hatp_hardware_credential_admin_script.py (28/28 pass, recover-specific tests converted to absence/retry tests, RECOVERY EVIDENCE assertions removed), tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7o_2l_1_hatp_trust_enrollment_admin_entrypoint_implementation.py (28/28 pass, recover-presence assertions converted to recover-absence assertions), tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7o_2l_2_hatp_trust_enrollment_admin_entrypoint_independent_verification.py (20/20 pass -- the historical fabricated-evidence exploit test now proves the identical attempt fails at argparse parsing in the repaired tree while its docstring preserves the original finding's full narrative; the vulnerable code remains permanently inspectable in git history at commit ab12406e). Combined focused suite across all five files: 134/134 pass. fast_green was run twice for comparison under python -m pytest -m fast_green -n auto -q: a git-stash-isolated pre-repair baseline (333 failed, 8472 passed, 4 skipped, 9 errors) versus the candidate working tree pre-commit (345 failed, 8486 passed, 4 skipped, 9 errors). A full node-ID diff of both raw FAILED/ERROR lists found exactly 12 tests present as failures only in the candidate run and zero tests present only in the baseline. All 12 were individually classified as non-attributable: 8 are git-status dirty-working-tree checks (asserting scripts/ or src/pcae/ has no uncommitted changes) that failed only because this phase's own scripts/hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py change was uncommitted at comparison time -- each assertion's source was inspected directly to confirm this, and all 8 were re-run individually post-commit and now pass; 2 (tests/test_backend_cli.py::TestBackendReviewReject::test_reject_updates_latest and tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7o_2l_7o_2k_3...::test_activate_on_unknown_id_fails_closed) were re-run individually outside the -n auto parallel split and passed cleanly, confirming pytest-xdist-parallel flakiness unrelated to any file this phase touched. Zero attributable regressions. Finding status: HARDWARE-ENROLLMENT RECOVERY AUTHORITY DEFECT -- REPAIRED, INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING (not self-closed; closure requires 149O.20L.7O.2L.4). No physical FIDO2/PIV hardware was touched in any test (every provider/ceremony interaction is a synthetic monkeypatched seam); no HardwareCredentialRecord/Principal/Signer/DeploymentBinding was created on any production/protected path (every writer call in this phase's own tests targets a disposable tmp_path root); no HMIC source scope was changed (_FROZEN_AUTHORITY_BEARING_FILES remains exactly 36); no Dell host was connected to or mutated; no HATP readiness/activation state was changed; runtime remained Observed/observe/unavailable throughout (confirmed via pcae runtime inspect). pcae health healthy, pcae check passed, pcae status coherence coherent, pcae doctor task-memory warnings (pre-existing, unrelated), pcae push check clean post-commit, pcae notify status Telegram configured.

test_results.primary_source_reread: Independently re-read HHCE-001 v1.1 full text (section 11, HHCE-REQ-015/016/017), the 149O.20L.7O.2L architecture-freeze document (sections 4-6), and the pre-repair scripts/hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py and src/pcae/core/hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py directly -- confirming no public recovery command is contract-required and register_credential idempotency exists for identical-evidence retry, before making any edit.
test_results.exact_source_change: Removed the recover argparse subcommand, its five CLI arguments, _cmd_recover, the recover dispatch branch, and _print_recovery_evidence from scripts/hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py. Added _register_with_in_process_retry (3-attempt bounded retry of register_credential against the identical provider-generated evidence), wired into _cmd_enroll. No core writer or contract file touched.
test_results.recover_removal_proof: Public CLI subcommands are exactly {enroll, revoke} (argparse-choices-asserted); any recover invocation fails at argument parsing (SystemExit code 2) before any provider/writer call; --help output never mentions recover; no _cmd_recover function or 'recover' string-literal subcommand name remains in the AST.
test_results.fabricated_evidence_rejection_proof: No CLI path under any subcommand accepts caller-supplied signer_key_id/public_key_hex/algorithm/protocol_name for record creation (mechanical argparse-dest search); the identical fabricated-evidence values from 2L.2's own historical exploit test now fail at argparse parsing with zero registry write.
test_results.enroll_call_count_proof: With a flaky register_credential (fails once, then succeeds), _run_enrollment_ceremony is called exactly once and register_credential is called exactly twice with the identical (is-compared) evidence object -- no second makeCredential ceremony under retry.
test_results.hardware_success_persistence_failure_mat: Never-landed write lands on retry (record active); already-landed write with a simulated post-write ack failure resolves idempotently via ALREADY_REGISTERED (no duplicate); a genuine differing-evidence conflict fails closed identically on every attempt, never overwriting the existing record; exhausted retries print a diagnostic naming no credential material and fail closed (exit 1).
test_results.revoke_regression: revoke still revokes an existing active record (exit 0, outcome=revoked) and a declined confirmation still makes zero writer calls -- _cmd_revoke/revoke_parser wiring unmodified by this repair.
test_results.principal_signer_unchanged_proof: scripts/hatp_principal_signer_admin.py git-diff-asserted byte-identical since phase entry; its public surface remains exactly enroll-principal/revoke-principal/enroll-signer/revoke-signer.
test_results.thin_wrapper_proof: No json/fcntl primitives anywhere in the script; the new retry helper's own AST call set is exactly {register_credential, print, range, len, type} -- a thin call-and-catch loop, not a reimplemented transaction engine; pcae.core.* imports unchanged.
